Equality forces one minimizing support, giving all tangent facet normals; cycle coverage k+c gives the n=3,4,>=5 split. Every outer vertex is a signed endpoint assignment; strict exchange improvement sorts maximizing loads and cycle independent-set counting yields R² and every contact count. Independent reflections and cyclic permutation force the unique John and Löwner ellipsoids to be concentric balls. All domains, equality conditions and boundaries are included. The extracted standard-library verifier corroborates 288399 exact assertions, without being substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 source defines this sum class and supplies subset inequalities that imply the general inradius reduction; that corollary is expressly not treated as novel. The proposed complete all-order cyclic John/Löwner ellipsoid, tangent-facet orbit, farthest-vertex and exact parity-count classification is not stated in its inspected full text. Searches and mathematical-record comparisons for near-congruent root/graphic bodies found no stronger theorem implying this result; distinction of Minkowski sums of coordinate diamonds from convex hulls of edge roots and sums of root-direction segments is essential. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The general inradius formula is already implied by published subset inequalities and is cited as such; only the combined cycle classification is put forward as new.
An unindexed treatment of signed graphical permutohedra or a stronger result hidden in a source available only in abstract could already imply some cyclic contact formulas.
Historical priority requires independent subject-matter review; no negative search can certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: The newly studied Minkowski-sum family has a canonical cyclic subfamily with explicit symmetry but nontrivial facet and vertex combinatorics. This complete all-dimensional metric classification specifies both extremal ellipsoids, all touching facet/vertex orbits, and a genuine parity split in farthest vertices, not just an isolated numerical special case. The hypergraph load-order lemma supplies a reusable combinatorial route to other outer radii. The known general subset inequality is acknowledged rather than offered as a novel contribution.
